key: must:A03d:Address preserves en dash, period, apostrophe, commas
symptom: Address preserves en dash, period, apostrophe, commas

whys.why: Why was the 'en dash, period, apostrophe, commas' item not met in either chat?
whys.because: In the new chat, the address on the flyer is garbled, so the grader cannot read any of its punctuation. In the old chat, the flyer has no address at all.
whys.evidence: s1.new.stupid.A03d/grade.json: 'Cannot be read; the address is garbled', with the address read as 'Unit 14B, [garbled] / Old Foundry ... [garbled] / Kingston upon Thames, KT1 20A6'. s1.old.stupid.A03d/grade.json: 'No address.'

whys.why: Why does the old flyer have no address?
whys.because: The stupid persona's first message gives no text: 'make a flyer for a printmakers open studio'. The old assistant did not ask which words to show. It called generate_image at once with words it made up ('OPEN STUDIO', 'Printmakers', 'Live demos • Prints for sale • All welcome'). It asked for the studio name, date, time and address only after it had delivered the flyer.
whys.evidence: s1.old.stupid.A03d/chat.json: messages[0] is 'make a flyer for a printmakers open studio'. calls.jsonl line 2: the generate_image prompt contains only invented text. Line 5: the delivered reply says 'Send me your studio name, date, time and address'.

whys.why: In the new build, the assistant did get the exact address and sent it in the prompt. Why is it garbled anyway?
whys.because: The assistant sent the full address with correct punctuation (an en dash in 127–129, 'St. John’s' with a curly apostrophe). But it asked for the address 'At the bottom in smaller text' on a 640px, 9:16 canvas. The output is 352×640, so the address lines are only a few pixels tall. At that size, qwen-image draws text-like scribbles instead of letters.
whys.evidence: s1.new.stupid.A03d/calls.jsonl line 11: resolution '640px', aspect_ratio '9:16', prompt '...At the bottom in smaller text: Unit 14B, Second Floor, ... 127–129 St. John’s Road...'. grade.json checks: '352x640'. assets/01-wait_for_image_project.png: the headline, date and time are crisp; the three tiny address lines are illegible ('Old Gunpowder...', 'KT1 20A6').

whys.why: Why was the canvas so small and narrow?
whys.because: 640px is the largest resolution the free plan allows. Also, plan_request returned aspect '9:16' with source 'user' ('the user's words'), but the user never gave a shape. A 9:16 canvas is narrower than the 4:5 in the brief, so the long address lines have even less width.
whys.evidence: Old calls.jsonl line 5 and new calls.jsonl line 14: '640px... the largest your free plan allows'. New calls.jsonl line 2: plan_request output gives aspect value '9:16', source 'user', from 'the user's words', but the user had only said 'make a flyer...'.

whys.why: Why did no tool stop or reroute a long exact line that must be small?
whys.because: Neither build warns that a line of about 100 characters in small type at 640px will not render. Neither build offers a way to put exact text on the image as deterministic text instead of model-drawn text. plan_request only gathers exact_words; it does not check whether they will be legible. The assistant suggested 'make the artwork with no text and add your words in an editor' only after it had delivered.
whys.evidence: tools-new.json plan_request description: 'exact_words is a list of strings... exactly as the user wrote it', with nothing about length or legibility. New calls.jsonl line 14: the assistant warns 'AI image models often get long text wrong, especially a long address' only after generation.

result.axiom: A diffusion image model (qwen-image-2.1) cannot reliably draw a long string of about 100 characters with exact punctuation in small type on a free-plan canvas of at most 640px. Below a few pixels of glyph height, it draws letter-like scribbles. This is a limit of the generation model and the free plan. (In the old chat, the address never reached the model, because the assistant did not ask which words to show.)
result.fix: When exact_words contains a line longer than about 40 characters (or more than about 60 characters in total), plan_request/generate_image should return a warning. They should then make the artwork without that text and add the exact lines server-side as real text (a deterministic text overlay), in a size that is legible at 640px. Also stop plan_request from filling in aspect '9:16' as 'user' when the user gave no shape. The old build also needs to ask which exact words to show before it generates a flyer.
